notices.title: Manchester International Airport Phase 2 - Overbridge Civils
notices.description: The planned introduction of longer train services to the Airport in response to future demand growth will mean that double stacking arrangements of trains as currently used will no longer be viable. Through the project's Delivery Steering Group, Northern and TransPennine Express have carried out analysis which has identified that additional platform capacity is needed at the airport in order to realise the full benefit of longer train services serving the airport. The scheme is part of a package of proposed measures in the Manchester area that are being designed/planned to boost capacity and resilience, emanating from the Cross Manchester Capacity and Reliability Improvement Study. Improving the operation of train services in the centre of Manchester and providing further capacity at Manchester Airport station, aligns with the strategic aims of Network Rail, TfGM, TfN and the wider industry. This project in in Tranche 1 of the Manchester and North West Transformation Programme (MNTP): A remodelling of the station at Manchester Airport, specifically a platform addition or extension of multiple platforms, or provision of a new turnback facility, will be essential to accommodate the planned implementation of longer rolling stock services. The redevelopment of these platforms will enable permissive working of two 6x24m (144m) trains, in two of the four platforms at the Airport Station. This will allow for the unaltered retention of all existing TOC services both originating and terminating at the Airport Station under 'double-stacking' conditions. The works comprise the construction and completion of the bridge structure and associated highway infrastructure, including: • Installation of client-supplied precast bridge components, including cills, beams and side walls, together with associated shear key reinforcement and grout connections. • Modification of existing bridge cill. • Supply and installation of bridge bearing plates, including associated screed works. • Construction of pile caps/infill. • Placement of in-situ concrete shear key infill. • Construction of the reinforced concrete bridge deck slab. • Construction of reinforced concrete parapet walls. • Placement of in-situ concrete footpaths and fill areas. • Construction of pilasters, including reinforced concrete and brickwork elements. • Supply and installation of parapet and pilaster copings. • Construction of associated fencing, signage and PCC retaining wall. • Installation of associated ducting works. • Completion of highway works excluding final road surfacing. • Application of bridge waterproofing systems, installation of expansion joints, and completion of associated sealing and mastic works. • Construction of associated drainage works. Exclusions: Final road/footpath surfacing works are excluded from this scope.

notices.title: DNWP0016 - WAGR Enabling Works and Strip-out - Sellafield - A2R JV
notices.description: WAGR Overview and Site Information The Windscale Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (WAGR), commissioned in 1962, was the prototype for the UK's second-generation Advanced Gas-cooled Reactor (AGR) fleet. The facility (Building B50), recognised by its distinctive spherical containment shell, was supported by the fuel assembly building (B52) and turbine hall (B55). Following reactor core dismantling and removal in 2012, the WAGR Complex entered Care and Maintenance (C&M). The facility is now progressing towards its final phase of decommissioning and demolition. Existing records confirm the presence of Low-Level Waste (LLW) and Intermediate-Level Waste (ILW), resulting in ongoing radiological and contamination hazards. All buildings within the WAGR area are owned by the Remediation operating unit, remain under active surveillance and maintenance, and are classified as Beta Gamma contamination facilities. Project Scope The scope comprises enabling, strip-out, waste management and decommissioning support activities across the WAGR facility, alongside support for wider Windscale decommissioning programmes and emergent operational requirements. Key activities include (see attachment) - Strip-out Works: Internal and external removal of fixtures, fittings, equipment and non-structural elements to facilitate future decommissioning and demolition activities. - Radiological Waste Management: Safe handling, removal and management of LLW and ILW in accordance with site requirements. - Asset Reinstatement: Delivery of asset reinstatement works and provision of SQEP resources to support successful handover. - Pre-Construction Information (PCI): Support information gathering and site characterisation where existing PCI is insufficient. - Surveys: Plan and undertake surveys to assess radiological, hazardous and operational conditions in support of future decommissioning works. - Project Enabling Works: Design, fabricate, trial and implement enabling solutions, equipment and materials to support project delivery. - Asbestos Management: Planning, sampling, monitoring and licensed asbestos removal where required. - Procurement: Procurement of materials, equipment and associated quality documentation. - Waste Management: Sorting, segregation, consolidation and disposal of current and historical wastes, including completion of documentation for transfer to Sellafield Waste Coordinators. - Emergent Works: Rapid response support to operations and maintenance teams for safety-critical issues. - Temporary Works: Management, design and construction of temporary works, including scaffolding, enclosures and other supporting structures. - Decontamination: Decontamination activities to support area declassification and radiological rollback. - Plant Modifications: Production of Plant Modification Proposals (PMPs) and associated documentation. - Scaffolding Services: Provision of scaffolding design, supply and installation resources as required.

notices.title: BBV Sublot 4 - HSST1020 - Cut & Bent Steel Reinforcement - Curzon Approach Viaducts
notices.description: This scope is for the provision of cut and bent steel reinforcement for Curzon Approach Viaducts. The supplier should review the steel reinforcement drawings and cut and bent steel in accordance with the drawings and bar bending schedules provided by the Contractor. Bars should be delivered to site labelled with the references of the bar bending schedule and pre-slung to facilitate safe unloading. Supplier should also provide any method statements and their related risk assessment as well as all relevant quality documentation such as quality management plan, grade mill certificates for the supplied re-bar, CARES certificates, CARS certificates and technical data sheets for the couplers, samples for testing (if required) and any other required to demonstrate compliance with the specification and industry standards. The package covers three key activities spanning over the next 2 and half years. These are the construction of the complex Curzon no. 3 post tensioned reinforced concrete deck and its finishes with 6220m3 of concrete and 2384tonnes of reinforcement remaining, the construction of the deck finishing works across the remaining assets of Curzon Approach (Curzon no. 2, Curzon no. 1 and Duddeston Viaduct) with ....tonnes remaining and the fabrication of the precast concrete slabs for Curzon Approach at BBV Kingsbury Yard with ....tonnes remaining.

notices.title: Strategic Defence Review - Energetics Grant Structure Information notice
notices.description: The UK government is acting on the Strategic Defence Review's recommendations by investing in the 'factories of the future' initiative, bringing energetics industries back to the UK, and strengthening our long-term national security by building up to six new energetics and munitions factories in the UK. The purpose of this notice is to communicate the Ministry of Defence's (MoD's) intention to open grant windows to support the construction of new energetic synthesis facilities. The MoD expects there to be multiple grant windows, during which companies may submit grant proposals. The grants are designed to establish new, sustainable UK production capacity for critical energetic materials. We are seeking to strengthen the resilience and security of our munitions supply chain, reduce reliance on overseas sources and unlock significant private investment in UK manufacturing. Advertisement of these grants will take place on the UK Government Find a Grant portal which will then provide a link to the application form on the Defence Sourcing Portal. Any company can apply to any or all investment windows regardless of having prior engagement with MoD however only one grant per project will be awarded. The first of these windows is planned to open imminently: This window will be open to applications for 6 weeks after which a down selection will take place based on the information provided in the application form. Those companies taken forward will be invited to further engage with the MoD to carry out due diligence and develop a grant award structure with the intention to issue Grant award letters to the successful companies within this fiscal year. Individual proposals will be eligible for grants of up to £45 million or 50% of the overall cost, whichever is smaller. The overall level of investment will depend on the quality and value for money assessment of proposals received, with funding decisions taken across the programme to ensure investment is targeted where it can deliver the greatest strategic benefit. Companies with credible proposals to invest in new UK energetic materials production capability are encouraged to apply. The grant competition is separate from the feasibility and engineering-design work already under way, and companies do not need to have participated in those earlier stages to apply. Proposals will need to demonstrate that they are technically credible, economically viable and capable of delivering strategically important UK production capability. Further grant windows are expected in Q2 and Q4 of 2027, however these are dependent on MoD need and may be subject to change. MoD investment will sit alongside the wider support opportunities offered by HM Government as set out in previous communications with industry.

notices.title: Project BRACIS
notices.description: The Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Delivery Team (CBRN DT) within the UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) has extended a single source Contract with Bruhn Newtech Ltd (BNT Ltd) for the support of Biological, Radiological and Chemical (BRaCIS) Warning and Reporting (W&R) software for a period of 4 years to FY 2030 with 1 x option year until 2031 to provide a continuing requirement to support the In-Service CBRN W&R software including training for UK Defence. A VTN was published for transparency purposes. It is considered that this extension to contract can be awarded using the negotiated procedure without prior publication of a contract notice, pursuant to Regulation 16(1)(a)(ii) of the UK Defence and Security Public Contract Regulations 2011 (No 1848), for technical reasons. BRaCIS software is owned, designed and maintained by BNT Ltd, the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). Despite the W&R software being a Commercial of The Shelf (COTS) item used by additional NATO countries, this software with BNT Ltd has been modified to meet the UK bespoke requirements defined by the UK MOD. These modifications are essential to make it compatible with the UK Defence BOWMAN ComBAT Information Platform (BCiP), operating on the BCiP networking platform. BRaCIS has been tested and verified by Dstl making this a bespoke capability for UK Defence which meets the UK CBRN W&R requirements and only BNT Ltd are able to provide BRaCIS and the in-service support. BRaCIS is essential to provide command and control where CBRN is an aspect of operations. NATO sets common standards for CBRN W&R software and BNT Ltd is the only provider who is also a member of the committee that manage updates to the NATO standards ATP - 45 (F). The use of a CBRN W&R software if not compliant with the NATO standards, would result in delays in receiving warning of a CBRN attack, which would result in a risk to life.

notices.title: Conversion of Storm Shelter into Public Convenience Facilities and Refurbishment of Accessible Toilet Accommodation, Blenheim Gardens, Minehead
notices.description: Minehead Town Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit tenders for the conversion of the former storm shelter within Blenheim Gardens, Minehead into modern public convenience facilities together with the refurbishment and conversion of a separate toilet building within the gardens to provide fully accessible toilet accommodation and associated storage facilities. The site occupies a prominent position within Blenheim Gardens, Minehead's principal public open space, and lies within the Wellington Square Conservation Area. The Council wishes to deliver attractive, durable, accessible and vandal-resistant facilities whilst preserving the architectural character and appearance of the existing buildings. The works comprise the alteration, refurbishment and fit out of two existing buildings. The former storm shelter will be converted to provide male and female public toilet accommodation, baby changing facilities and associated handwashing facilities. A separate building within the gardens will be refurbished to provide a fully accessible toilet facility together with independent storage accommodation. The project includes, but is not limited to, demolition and alteration works, drainage works, utility connections, plumbing and sanitary installations, electrical installations, ventilation systems, roofing replacement and repairs, internal finishes, accessibility improvements, external repairs, testing, commissioning and all associated works necessary to provide fully operational public convenience facilities. The successful contractor will be responsible for providing all labour, materials, plant, supervision and specialist subcontractors required to complete the works. Responsibilities will include project management, utility provider liaison, Building Regulations compliance, testing, commissioning, certification and handover. Particular emphasis is placed upon durability, long-term maintainability, accessibility and resistance to vandalism. Materials, fixtures, fittings and finishes must be suitable for intensive public use and capable of withstanding a coastal environment exposed to wind-driven rain, salt-laden air and high seasonal visitor numbers. Tenderers shall demonstrate relevant experience in the successful delivery of comparable construction and refurbishment projects and provide evidence of their ability to meet programme requirements. The completed facilities must be fully operational and available for public use no later than 1 March 2027. The Council reserves the right not to accept the lowest or any tender received and reserves the right to amend, suspend, abandon or recommence the procurement process at any stage.

notices.title: Dungavel House IRC - Defective Roof and Basement Refurbishment - BPRN 370279/7129
notices.description: Originally investigating for the presence of reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete(RRAC) within the main house building at Dungavel IRC, a visual inspection was carried out in March 2024 to define the buildings structural condition. Despite no indication of the presence of RRAC, the inspection identified the poor structural condition of the roof, and the significant deflection and distortion of the two built-up steel girders, the ends of which were partially being pulled out of the brickwork walls. This girder had deflected beyond a serviceable state whilst the ridge beam's timer support post also showed significant defects which included a disconnected knee brace timber. A subsequent visual inspection carried out in November 2024 identified significant water ingress issues within the basement below the main house building. The water ingress was understood to be a longstanding issue and has caused water-related damage to structural elements within the basement. Neither the source nor the cause of the water ingress is currently known. The defective roof and water ingress issues within the basement pose major structural Health and Safety concerns. The Home Office seeks to undertake a refurbishment to address any non-compliant areas and disrepair of the roof and basement in the main house building at Dungavel IRC.

notices.title: Swanley Park Footpath Refurbishment
notices.description: Swanley Town Council is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the excavation, removal, reconstruction and improvement of two existing footpaths. The project aims to improve accessibility, durability and the overall quality of the footpath network through the installation of wider, fit-for-purpose pathways that meet the requirements of their intended use. The works will comprise the following: Footpath One Footpath One extends approximately 355.4 linear metres and will broadly follow the alignment of the existing footpath. The pathway will be widened to provide a finished width of approximately 2.5 metres, excluding edging. The construction must be suitable for occasional vehicular access, with the appropriate sub-base and construction specification provided to accommodate this requirement. Footpath Two Footpath Two currently measures approximately 29 linear metres and will be extended to approximately 62.3 linear metres. The completed pathway will provide a finished width of approximately 2 metres, excluding edging, improving the provision and usability of the route. Surfacing Options and Construction Requirements The Council is currently exploring a range of surfacing options for the proposed footpaths, including self-binding gravel, tarmac and block paving. Contractors may be required to consider the suitability, durability, maintenance requirements, accessibility and whole-life costs associated with these options to help inform the Council's final decision on the preferred surfacing materials. The appointed contractor will be expected to undertake the necessary excavation and removal of existing footpath materials, prepare the underlying formation, install an appropriate sub-base and construct the new footpaths in accordance with the agreed specification. The works will also include suitable edging, finishing details and any associated reinstatement required to leave the completed pathways in a safe, stable and serviceable condition. All works must be carried out to an appropriate professional standard, with due consideration given to site conditions, public safety, drainage, accessibility and the long-term performance of the finished surfaces. The contractor will be responsible for ensuring that the construction methods and materials used are suitable for the intended use of each footpath. The Council is seeking a cost-effective and durable solution that provides improved pedestrian routes, meets the operational requirements of the site and offers good long-term value for money. notices.title: Petrus Clean and Clear Services
notices.description: This contract provides a comprehensive Clean and Clear service designed to support the management, maintenance and re-letting of residential properties and communal areas. The service includes the clearance, removal and lawful disposal of furniture, household goods, personal belongings, general waste, fly-tipped materials, bulky items and other unwanted contents from occupied properties, void properties, communal areas, garages, stores, gardens, external land and associated premises. The scope covers internal and external property clearances, including emergency and responsive works where properties require urgent attention due to abandonment, hoarding, antisocial behaviour, tenancy termination, health and safety concerns or preparation for refurbishment and reoccupation. All waste and materials are to be removed, transported and disposed of in accordance with applicable environmental legislation and waste management requirements, with recycling undertaken wherever reasonably practicable. The service also includes specialist cleaning and property preparation works. These may comprise general cleaning, deep cleaning, sparkle cleans, sanitary cleaning, biohazard cleaning, trauma cleaning, pest-related cleaning and the removal of hazardous materials where appropriately licensed and authorised. Needle sweeps and the safe collection, handling and disposal of sharps and associated hazardous waste form part of the service requirements. In addition to clearance and cleaning activities, the contractor shall provide a range of minor property repair and make-ready services designed to return properties to a safe, clean and lettable condition. Works may include internal and external redecoration, patch repairs, preparation of surfaces, replacement or repair of floor coverings, removal and replacement of damaged fixtures and fittings, minor joinery, handyman repairs and other associated remedial works as instructed. The service may be delivered to individual properties, blocks, estates and communal environments across the contracting authority's operational area. Works may include garden and external area clearance, vegetation removal, shed and outbuilding clearance, removal of debris, litter picking and the clearance of waste from communal spaces. The contractor will be expected to provide a flexible and responsive service, including routine, urgent and emergency call-out requirements, working closely with housing, neighbourhood, maintenance and void management teams. The objective of the contract is to provide an efficient, high-quality and value-for-money solution that supports neighbourhood improvements, reduces void turnaround times, addresses environmental concerns and ensures properties and communal areas are maintained in a safe, clean and presentable condition suitable for occupation, inspection, refurbishment or ongoing use.

notices.title: DN731976 Lift Modernisation Framework Agreement
notices.description: Hackney Council Seek to establish a Lift Modernisation Framework of experienced and competent Lift Contractors. The purpose of this framework is to deliver ambitious annual programmes of work to drive modernisation across the lift stock, by appointing up to three (3) lift contractors to work simultaneously across all regions of Hackney and Hackneys housing stock. The aim is to reduce future maintenance cost and breakdowns and as well as aid in improving the quality of our lift service for our residents and tenants. Hackney have in excess of 600 lifts within its housing stock. A total of 39 priority lifts have already been identified for renewal. In order to improve the overall percentage of modernisation across the stock, these first 39 lifts form a programme of work that has been included as part of the tender process. Potential bidders will be required to price up a programme that include these 39 priority lifts, as part of their tender commercial submission. The 39 lifts will be split into 3 programmes of work. Each Bidder appointed to the Framework will be awarded one Year 1 Programme of work in order to front load programme delivery and commence work on site as quickly as possible. The top three scoring Bidders in the tender process will be appointed to the Framework. Following further evaluation of individual programme costs and quality scores, each Framework Contractor will then be awarded one programme of work. Each contractor appointed to the framework will be allocated a programme of between 11 - 15 lifts for refurbishment, which will effectively form the first 12 month programme of work. Each programme can include any regions and wards across Hackney. Future works programmes will be awarded based on individual contractors' overall performance, initially based on delivery KPIs during the first 9 months. In addition to the Housing Lift stock, this framework may also include ad hoc lift modernisation and renewal work from other departments across Hackney Council, for example corporate and education buildings.The framework would also allow provision for mini competition if required. Hackney Council requires experienced and competent lift contractors to be appointed to the Framework. Therefore all Bidders must be a member of a recognised lift industry association such as LEIA (Lift Engineering Industry Association). Terms It is anticipated that there will be up to £28,000,000 worth of spend during the full potential term of the framework agreement. It is envisaged that there will be between 18 to 45 lift modernisation projects delivered each year, split across 3 programmes. It is anticipated that each Framework Contractor will be awarded 1 programme of work each year. This will be subject to budget and framework capacity and performance. notices.title: Manchester International Airport - Rail Footprint Civils
notices.description: The planned introduction of longer train services to the Airport in response to future demand growth will mean that double stacking arrangements of trains as currently used will no longer be viable. Through the project's Delivery Steering Group, Northern and TransPennine Express have carried out analysis which has identified that additional platform capacity is needed at the airport in order to realise the full benefit of longer train services serving the airport. The scheme is part of a package of proposed measures in the Manchester area that are being designed/planned to boost capacity and resilience, emanating from the Cross Manchester Capacity and Reliability Improvement Study. Improving the operation of train services in the centre of Manchester and providing further capacity at Manchester Airport station, aligns with the strategic aims of Network Rail, TfGM, TfN and the wider industry. This project in in Tranche 1 of the Manchester and North West Transformation Programme (MNTP): A remodelling of the station at Manchester Airport, specifically a platform addition or extension of multiple platforms, or provision of a new turnback facility, will be essential to accommodate the planned implementation of longer rolling stock services. The redevelopment of these platforms will enable permissive working of two 6x24m (144m) trains, in two of the four platforms at the Airport Station. This will allow for the unaltered retention of all existing TOC services both originating and terminating at the Airport Station under 'double-stacking' conditions. The scope areas for this package are as follows: - OLE Substructures & Foundations - King Post Retaining Walls - Ancillary Civils (Inclusive of but not limited to; Trough routes, small concrete foundations, UTX's and signage).

notices.title: S30141 Technical Standards Implementation, Governance improvements and benefit realisation
notices.description: National Highways has a statutory obligation under the Technical Regulations Protocol to keep its technical standards, the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges (DMRB) and the Manual of Contract Documents for Highway Works (MCHW) up to date. Maintaining these standards creates opportunities to improve the efficiency, safety and consistency of design, construction and maintenance activities, aligning delivery with the organisation's strategic objectives. Building on the extensive refresh programmes completed in RIS1 and RIS2, the focus in RIS3 shifts from redevelopment to effective implementation and embedment of the revised DMRB and MCHW, including the introduction of proportionate mitigation measures, strengthened governance arrangements, and supporting digital tools to ensure consistent application across the sector. The proposed task will modernise National Highways technical standards management over RIS3 and beyond. It will enable more efficient updating, faster publication, and consolidation of changes made in RIS1 and RIS2. It will support continuous digitisation, restructuring of our technical standards, enhancements of digital tools, which will make it significantly easier for technical authors to develop standards, apply the drafting rules and the overall governance framework for technical standards. Enhancements to the standard governance will include clearer more accessible author guidance. This will improve both transparency and inclusivity across the standards development lifecycle.

notices.description: The former RAF and fire training facility at Manston has been utilised by the Home Office for the past 12 months and requires redevelopment to suit its current needs. The Home Office have identified a need to reconfigure the current layout of the accommodation and facilities and further redevelop the existing Manston site. The proposed new development will provide improved accommodation and facilities that will support a more effective operation and replace the current temporary facilities. Demolition forms part of the enabling works to achieve this. The overall scope of works is as outlined below (list not exhaustive): - Development of a demolition plan - Undertaking statutory notifications for asbestos removal - Asbestos Removal - Demolition of the H-Block and Blues and Twos buildings (Building's 004, 131, 010, 045 & 044A) - Demolition of associated footings, foundations and redundant services - Incorporation of sequenced demolition and crushing of the superstructures of buildings on the site - Coordinated below grade level removal - Coordinating with the UXO nominated consultant and utilities designer.
